To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the organic matter preserved in the early Albian OAE1b black shale is dominated by archaeal remains and that this organic matter was produced by chemoautotrophic archaea living in an anoxic water column.
archaea were a major source of organic matter during the early Albian OAE1b.
archaeal remains are the main source for the insoluble organic matter in OAE1b black shale sediments.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the origin of organic matter in black shales of an oceanic anoxic episode and the causes for 13 C-enrichment of the organic carbon.

the identification and quantification of the sources of organic matter in black shales of early Albian OAE1b, which are characterized by a high organic carbon (OC), low carbonate content and distinct lamination.
the origin of the black shale organic matter and the 13C-environmental isotope signature of OAE1B.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the black shale of OAE1 is a product of the deposition of organic matter derived predominantly from chemoautotrophic archaea in a highly stratified water column, whereas the black shale of the Cenoman/Turon OAE is a product of deposition of organic matter of phytoplankton origin under anoxic conditions in a water column that was only weakly stratified.

the early Albian OAE1b black shale formation was not caused by a major increase of marine phytoplankton production, but was the result of a major increase of archaea-derived organic matter production.
the early Albian OAE 1b black shale deposits are the first unequivocal evidence for a significant contribution of archaea to the global carbon cycle.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
archaeal remains are abundant in the early Albian black shales and that they were the dominant source of the organic matter in these sediments, which were deposited under anoxic conditions.

the organic matter of both the early Albian OAE1b black shale of the SEFB (France) and the ODP site 1099C black shale (off Florida) is dominated by archaea, which were living as chemoautotrophic planktonic organisms.
the black shales from OAE1b are dominated by archaeal organic matter, whereas the black shales associated with OAE2 are predominantly derived from algal organic matter.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the early Albian OAE1b black shale organic matter is dominated by archaea and that the organic matter of this OAE is very different from that of the Cenomanan/Turonian OAE.
the early Albian black shales of both ODP site 1094C and the Ravel Section of the SEFB were formed by anoxic conditions that allowed the preservation of archaeal organic matter.
archaea-derived organic matter is an important source of OC in marine sediments and that this contribution may have been even more important in the geological past than today.
